slides.title: Decorators with Arguments Architecture
slides.prompt: To pass arguments to a decorator itself (e.g., `@repeat(num_times=3)`), you need three nested function layers: an outer factory function that accepts parameters, a middle decorator function, and an inner wrapper function.

slides.title: Outer Factory Layer
slides.prompt: Fill in the return statement for the outer factory function that delivers the decorator.

slides.title: Evaluation of Parametrized Decorators
slides.prompt: What does `@repeat(3)` evaluate to before receiving the decorated function?
options: It invokes `repeat(3)` which returns the actual decorator function (`decorator_repeat`)
It calls the decorated function 3 times immediately
It creates a tuple containing 3 function wrappers
It converts 3 into a string name
slides.correctAnswer: It invokes `repeat(3)` which returns the actual decorator function (`decorator_repeat`)

slides.title: Optional Argument Pattern
slides.prompt: Fill in the parameter default used to allow a decorator to be called with or without parentheses.

slides.title: Number of Nesting Levels Required
slides.prompt: How many function nesting levels are required for a standard decorator that accepts custom parameters?

slides.title: Keyword-Only Decorator Arguments
slides.prompt: Fill in the separator symbol used in the factory declaration to enforce keyword-only arguments.

slides.title: Decorator Factory Function Purpose
slides.prompt: What is the sole responsibility of the outermost function in a parametrized decorator?
options: To accept config arguments and return a customized decorator closure
To execute the underlying function with timeout limits
To override class constructor dunder methods
To validate function return type annotations
slides.correctAnswer: To accept config arguments and return a customized decorator closure
